text:
anya: quick idea — introduce a tiny "proof" emitted by gateways on compact ingest: claim_id + fingerprint + key_id. keeps compact records verifiable without holding full provenance.
ben: by "fingerprint" do you mean a deterministic hash over request metadata? small enough to store inline? :thinking_face:
anya: yep. e.g. sha256(model, tenant_id, root_request_id, token_counts, prefix_kv_trunc) then HMAC with gateway key. claim_id derived deterministically so retries dedupe.
carla: main worry is reorder/late provenance. if compact writes happen first, how do we reconcile when provenance arrives later?
dima: we can have a short unresolved TTL. emit an unresolved marker in the compact index. when provenance shows up, patch the record. if it never arrives within window, mark for full rehydrate on audit.
anya: exactly — two-tier: fast compact + eventual enrichment. fallback to full-rehydrate audit after 48h TTL.
ravi: billing/chargebacks require deterministic attribution. enrichment must not change claim_id mapping.
anya: claim_id = stable hash(root_request_id, ingest_shard, seq) so enrichment only enriches fields; billing always uses (claim_id, fingerprint) as source of truth. enc: (ben typo) operational q: what about key rotation? how will historical audits verify old HMACs?
carla: include key_id in proof. provenance service keeps rotation table and historical keys for audit verification. rotation retention must exceed audit window.
dima: perf: computing sha256+HMAC per request may be hot. do we measure?
ravi: microbench in gateway path. if hot, offload to sidecar that batches HMAC ops.
anya: will bench. proposed compact-proof shape:

```json
{
  "claim_id": "<str>",
  "fingerprint": "<hex>",
  "key_id": "k2024-07",
  "ts": "<epoch_ms>",
  "flags": ["compact","partial-provenance"]
}
```

carla: schema ok. add metrics: unresolved_compacts, patched_compacts, fallback_rehydrates. trace claim_id -> audit_id.
dima: backfills: when provenance arrives post-window emit a backfill event to audit queue with rehydrate hint. consumers must be idempotent keyed on claim_id.
anya: consumer dedupe by claim_id and include minor sequence to detect order flips.
ravi: can we reuse the existing chunked-handshake API? or new endpoint?
anya: reuse handshake API with mode=compact param to minimize surface area. easier to deploy.
ben: +1; add tenant opt-in flag for rollout (some customers might demand full provenance).
carla: rollout plan: default off, pilot internally, measure audit latency and storage savings. hook Redwood Optimize to detect attribution drift regressions.
metering-bot: deploy checklist: create perf ticket ENG-XXXX, add key-rotation playbook, verify historical key retention.
anya: i'll draft RFC follow-up with perf targets and schema, link to this thread. thanks all.
ben: small ask — log claim_id -> ingest_node for debugging.
dima: add unit tests for HMAC verification and chaos test simulating late provenance/backfill.
ravi: action: i'll run 10k rps bench on single gateway+sidecar and report CPU/latency.
anya: summary of tradeoffs in follow-up: faster reads and lower compact storage vs increased complexity in enrichment/backfill and reliance on key rotation and idempotent consumers.
